cosy-lesson.title: The Science of Sleep : Recalibrating the Mind

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Circadian rhythm – the natural, internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle, repeating roughly every 24 hours.

p.em: Example: Artificial blue light from screens disrupts your circadian rhythm, delaying melatonin production.

cosy-blockquote.p: Consolidation – the cognitive process where the brain stabilizes and organizes temporary memories into long-term storage.

p.em: Example: Deep sleep is absolutely critical for the consolidation of vocabulary words learned during the day.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insomnia – habitual sleeplessness or the persistent inability to fall asleep and stay asleep.

p.em: Example: High professional stress and digital overstimulation are the primary triggers of modern insomnia.

cosy-blockquote.p: Glymphatic system – the functional waste clearance system that cleanses the brain of metabolic waste during deep sleep.

p.em: Example: During deep sleep, the glymphatic system becomes highly active, flushing out toxic proteins.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive deficit – a reduction or impairment in mental capabilities, including focus, memory, and decision speed.

p.em: Example: Just one night of poor sleep introduces a severe cognitive deficit equivalent to mild intoxication.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deprivation – the state of lacking a basic necessity or biological requirement, such as sleep or food.

p.em: Example: Chronic sleep deprivation destroys emotional regulation, making individuals hyper-reactive to stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Somatic – relating to the body as distinct from the mind; physical manifestations of physiological stress.

p.em: Example: Chronic fatigue is a somatic manifestation of underlying neurological exhaustion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Restoration – the process of returning a system to its original, healthy, and fully functioning state.

p.em: Example: The primary purpose of slow-wave sleep is physical restoration and immune system repair.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stimulus – an environmental or sensory input that activates a physiological response or keeps the brain awake.

p.em: Example: Consuming caffeine in the late afternoon acts as a strong chemical stimulus that blocks sleep signals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habituate – to adapt, adjust, or become accustomed to a specific sleep schedule or routine over time.

p.em: Example: Once you habituate to waking up at dawn, your body will naturally align its hormone cycles.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does traveling across multiple time zones disrupt our biological Circadian rhythm ?
★ How sensitive is your personal sleep schedule to minor changes in your daily routine?

Why is deep, uninterrupted sleep essential for the Consolidation of newly acquired language skills?
★ What is your primary strategy for remembering complex information before a major exam or meeting?

How can we break the anxious psychological cycle of lying awake worrying about Insomnia ?
★ Have you ever suffered from temporary insomnia, and what was the root cause of your sleeplessness?

How does understanding the Glymphatic system change our view of sleep from a passive luxury to an active necessity?
★ Do you view sleeping eight hours as a strategic choice or a waste of productive time?

What is the most noticeable Cognitive deficit you experience when operating on less than six hours of sleep?
★ Have you ever made a major professional error due to simple fatigue and lack of focus?

What are the long-term psychological consequences of chronic sleep Deprivation on our emotional resilience?
★ How do you manage your mood and communication style when you are completely exhausted?

In what ways does a lack of deep rest translate into chronic, painful Somatic tension in the body?
★ Where in your body do you physically experience the effects of a poor night's sleep?

Why is psychological Restoration during dreaming sleep critical for processing traumatic emotional events?
★ Can you recall a vivid dream that seemed to help you process a real-life anxiety?

How can we remove sleep-disrupting Stimulus inputs from our bedrooms to optimize our hygiene?
★ What is your current evening routine, and how do you prepare your mind for restful sleep?

How long does it take for a person to Habituate to a non-traditional night-shift work schedule?
★ What is the ideal sleep schedule that makes you feel most energized and creative?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: The Sleep Manifesto: Imagine you are addressing a corporate board that expects employees to answer emails at midnight. Present your case for sleep optimization, using at least one second conditional, one third conditional, and one mixed conditional.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li: If you synchronized your lifestyle with your natural Circadian rhythm tomorrow, would your productivity double?
If you prioritized sleep consolidation, would you find learning a foreign language far easier today?
If you suffered from chronic Insomnia tomorrow, would you refuse to take sleep medication?
If the Glymphatic system stopped functioning during sleep, would our brains age rapidly today?
If you did not have a severe Cognitive deficit today, would you complete your tasks in half the time?
If we had not normalized chronic sleep Deprivation , would modern office cultures be less toxic today?
If your Somatic fatigue had been addressed years ago, would you now have more physical energy today?
If you had experienced deep psychological Restoration last night, would you feel less anxious today?
If we removed every digital Stimulus from our bedroom, would our sleep quality improve tonight?
If you managed to Habituate to waking up at dawn, would your overall lifestyle be healthier today?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am sleeping very bad → Correct: I sleep very poorly / I have been sleeping very poorly ((Grammar: use the adverb 'poorly' to modify the verb 'sleep' instead of the adjective 'bad'))

Incorrect: It is important to have a good sleep → Correct: It is important to get good sleep / It is important to sleep well ((Collocation error: we 'get good sleep' or 'sleep well', rather than 'having a good sleep'))

Incorrect: We discussed about our sleep habits → Correct: We discussed our sleep habits / had a discussion about our sleep habits ((Verb transitivity: 'discuss' is transitive and does not take 'about' directly))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Review language highlights and key corrections with your teacher.
